scope: isolated renderer characterization; no VoiceChat runtime integration

fixtures.short: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.
fixtures.medium: A fluent spoken assistant must begin responding before the complete answer has been generated. It must keep producing audio while text continues to arrive, and it must stop promptly when the user interrupts.
fixtures.long: The Strix serving study treats the conversational timeline as the product boundary. A speech renderer may be replaced if it accepts text quickly, starts audio incrementally, sustains real-time output, and drains or cancels without damaging conversation state. The useful comparison is therefore not model identity but the felt latency, continuity, and interruptibility of the resulting conversation.
